niche: a New Zealand building society's quarterly take-or-pay block of outsourced agent-hours for the calls to holders of maturing term deposits, where a conversation that goes to the retention offer is billed at 22 agent-minutes against 8 for a plain renewal and the January to March 2027 list is mostly the money the society's 2023 four-year new-money special won, meeting a moderate drop as the posted card turns up
answer: We should book 5,250 agent-hours with Harbourline for the 18,400 term deposits on the January to March 2027 maturity list: 1,250 for the deposits maturing in January, 2,000 for February and 2,000 for March.

spine.entity: one dial Harbourline made on a released case

driver: A behavioural share at a one-off repricing is a mixture of two kinds of unit, those a temporary price premium brought in, which take the costly path at their first repricing whatever the price change, and long-standing units, which take it in proportion to the change; conditioned on the price change alone, the share is read off a past in which the forward pool's change was met almost only by long-standing units, so it misses a forward pool made mostly of premium-won units, and only the class, rebuilt from each unit's price against the floor of its own entry cohort, makes every past round agree.
driver_concrete: Each conversation Harbourline holds with a maturing term deposit's holder goes to the 22-minute retention offer with a probability set by the class of the money: 87 per cent for money a new-money special won (a rate 0.40 points or more above the lowest of its term and opening quarter), at its first maturity and at every drop it met; about one in seven for member money, rising with the drop from its locked rate to Kaimai's posted card. January to March 2027 is 58 per cent the 2023 four-year special's money (10,697 deposits at 5.65 per cent, 0.50 above the 5.15 of their cohort) meeting a 1.65-point drop to the 4.00 per cent four-year card, a drop at which past conversations, almost all about member money, went to the offer about a third of the time, so classing the money books 5,250 agent-hours where the repricing-gap share books 4,250 and every pooled, latest, term, trend, locked-rate or fitted share 3,750 to 4,750.
stump: A competent solver washes the numbers, prices dialling per mix of callable numbers from the seven closed campaigns, conditions the past share of conversations that went to the retention offer on each deposit's drop from its locked rate to the card it reinvests at and books 4,250 agent-hours; the step that lands it there is reading that share off every past conversation at the drop instead of off the conversations of the same class of money: 10,697 of the 18,400 deposits are money the 2023 four-year special won at 5.65 per cent, and money a special won went to the offer at 87 per cent at its first maturity whatever its drop, where past conversations at the special's 1.65-point drop, almost all member money, went at a third: the golden is 5,250.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the SOW's billing and dialling rules, washes every number against the do-not-call register, prices dialling per mix of callable numbers with the release share and conditions the retention-offer share on each deposit's drop from its locked rate to the card it reinvests at books 4,250 agent-hours (4,267.1; pooled, latest campaign, locked rate or a logistic in the drop the same bin; the drop and term in one logistic 4,750; the locked rate by term 4,500; by term 3,750; split by first listing 4,250), at least two bins short of the golden 5,250.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the share of maturing term deposits whose holders, once reached, will move their money, which deposit-liquidity behaviour forecasts by the stability class of the money (rate-driven money a new-money special won against member money rolling on the posted card) as well as by the repricing gap; with insurance nouns a price change at renewal is the insurer's own and its size carries the renewal, while every deposit-taker's card moves with the cash rate, so a drop sends member money almost nowhere and only money that came for a special's premium leaves at its first maturity whatever its drop.

differentiation.task117: task117's forward peak turns on draw caps that belong to another entity reached through a dated join and on follow-on operations re-timed behind the one ahead (a queue's timing); here nothing is joined from another entity and nothing is re-timed: the share of conversations that go long is conditioned on how each deposit's money was won and on its repricing gap, and the forward figure is a sum over the list, not a peak.
differentiation.task37: task37's forward count is conditioned on a coupling to a linked entity's authorisation, recovered from a closed outcome roll as an absolute split no document states; here the split is the unit's own entry price against its cohort's floor, rebuilt from the lists, with no linked entity, and the past rounds' outcomes separate the classes at every price change.
differentiation.task44: task44's pooled pilot gain is a mixture of opposite effects split by a behavioural moderator measured over a prior instance of the window; here there is no pilot and no opposite effect: both classes leave more as the price falls, one at nine in ten at any drop, and the forward list's class mix is the shift.
differentiation.task97: task97's chance turns on the cumulative history of the place a unit occupies, counted across every occupant; here it turns on how the unit's own money was won and on its own price change at one repricing, and no place, occupant or history count enters.
differentiation.task138: task138's season order replays thirty past weather years from the depletion each field carries on 31 January 2027, a state rebuilt from each field's last delivery and the dry winter since; here no state is rebuilt or replayed: the share of conversations that go long is carried per class of money and band of drop onto a list whose class mix the past never carried at its drop.
differentiation.task95: task95's yield splits by a stand's age at first thinning, a class recovered by differencing two dated events across two registers, and the blended conversion is the default; here the default is the field's own repricing-gap model, which already conditions on the price change, and the class is how the unit's money was won (a special's premium over its entry cohort's posted rate), whose holders leave at their first repricing whatever the change while the rest leave in proportion to it.
differentiation.task20: task20's rate turns on whether each unit's commitment fence covers its supply lead time, a classification two large units moved across at renewal; here no unit moves class: the class is fixed by the price each deposit was won at, and the forward pool is a new cohort made mostly of one class at a change the past met almost only with the other.
differentiation.task137: round 1 conditioned the share on the repricing drop alone, which the strong model takes by reflex; round 2's decisive step is the class of money beside the drop, and the drop alone books 4,250 against the golden 5,250.

lineage.fate: superseded 2026-10-14 at round 2: the 10/10 audit (COMPLIANT_WEAK) found the repricing drop the strong model's reflex and the field's textbook model, a locked-rate-by-term logit landing the golden bin without the card, the locked-rate rung one bin under, Ask B's migration file announcing its overlap, Ask A's clause signalling its device and the swap test passing only narrowly; never on the portal
lineage.driver: A unit's chance of needing the long, costly form of a service at a one-off repricing is set by the gap between the price it locked in and the schedule it rolls onto, so the share is stable across past rounds only per unit of that gap; carried pooled, from the latest round, trended, by product group or by the unit's own locked price, it misses the coming round, whose dominant cohort meets a gap no past unit of its own group met, and every such carry understates the forward effort by a tenth to a quarter.
